stemMd: According to the passage, the organic fraction of a marsh's accumulated elevation

options.label: A
options.textMd: is larger than the mineral contribution in most marshes

options.label: B
options.textMd: is reduced when flooding becomes deep enough to stress marsh grasses

options.label: C
options.textMd: is unaffected by how deeply or how long a marsh floods

options.label: D
options.textMd: consists of mineral sediment carried onto the marsh by the tide

options.label: E
options.textMd: has fallen by more than half since 1950 in the estuaries Vogel surveyed

explanationMd:
An "according to the passage" question is a lookup, not an inference. Find the words the question names, then read the sentence they sit in.

**Step 1 — locate the term.** The passage defines the organic fraction in the first paragraph: the marsh "accumulates the roots and stems its own plants leave behind," and later, "the grasses whose litter becomes the organic fraction." So the organic fraction is plant material, not sediment.

**Step 2 — find where the passage says something happens to it.** The end of the second paragraph: when only "the organic half of the feedback remains," that half "is itself curtailed once flooding grows deep enough to stress the grasses." *Curtailed* means cut back.

**Step 3 — match.** One choice restates that sentence: the organic fraction **is reduced when flooding becomes deep enough to stress marsh grasses**. That is the answer.

**How to check.** Put your finger on the single clause that licenses the choice and read it aloud. Here it is "curtailed once flooding grows deep enough to stress the grasses" — one clause, one match. Then run the opposite test on the choice that looks most like a trap: the choice saying the organic fraction is *unaffected* by how deeply or how long a marsh floods is the direct negation of that same clause, so the two cannot both stand and the passage settles which survives. When one choice is the exact contradiction of another, the correct answer is almost always one of the two, and the passage will tell you which.

distractorRationale.c: This is the direct negation of the sentence that ends the second paragraph, which says the organic half is curtailed once flooding grows deep enough to stress the grasses. Flooding depth is precisely what the passage says does affect it.
distractorRationale.d: This swaps the two contributions the first paragraph is at pains to separate. Mineral sediment carried in on the tide is the other half of accretion; the organic fraction is the litter of the marsh's own plants.
distractorRationale.e: The more-than-half decline since 1950 is reported for the suspended load measured at the head of tide, a mineral quantity. Attaching that figure to the organic fraction transfers a statistic from the source the passage measured to one it never measured.
distractorRationale.a: The passage never ranks the two contributions by size. It describes how each is produced and how they are linked, but it offers no comparison of their magnitudes in any marsh, let alone in most marshes.

accessibilityText: Question about the passage on salt-marsh accretion and the sediment budget: identify what the passage says about the organic fraction of a marsh's accumulated elevation. The five choices state that it is reduced when flooding becomes deep enough to stress marsh grasses, that it consists of mineral sediment carried onto the marsh by the tide, that it has fallen by more than half since 1950 in the estuaries Vogel surveyed, that it is larger than the mineral contribution in most marshes, and that it is unaffected by how deeply or how long a marsh floods. Select one answer choice.

provenance.notes: Original Reading Comprehension item on the original passage gre-rc-marsh-accretion-300, written for the wave 4 top-up. Each wrong choice fails in a distinct, nameable way: direct negation, confusion of the two contributions, a statistic moved to the wrong quantity, and a comparison the passage never makes. Not adapted from any ETS item.

review.notes: Author solved as A on the clause 'a half that is itself curtailed once flooding grows deep enough to stress the grasses'. Uniqueness: B assigns the organic fraction the definition the passage gives the mineral one; C moves the suspended-load figure onto a quantity the survey did not measure; D requires a magnitude comparison the passage never makes; E is the explicit negation of the clause that licenses A. Awaiting blind independent solve; the author must not publish own work. Options were reordered after review to remove answer-position bias; ids and labels were remapped with the key.
